messages:
alex: heads up — noticed a slow GPU memory creep on prod-gpu-03 over the last ~24h. KV cache resident pages steadily increasing, periodic CUDA errors, and yesterday two containers OOM'd and restarted. Customers behind route /v1/chat are seeing aborted streams and 503s. filing here for triage.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0458 — High GPU memory growth on prod-gpu-03 (auto-detected by mem-sweep). PagerDuty: oncall@redwood > rafael acknowledged.

priya: quick triage notes — logs show paged-attention allocator reporting increasing "resident_pages" and a growing bitmap fragmentation. eviction loop isn't reclaiming as expected (evict_score stays < 0.2). seeing these repeated entries: 

```
W kv_cache: resident_pages=73248 free_pages=1024 fragmentation=0.86
E allocator: attempt_free failed, candidate_count=0
E cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (700)
```

Looks like slow drift: not an instant leak but fragmentation + slow siphon during warmup. Also seeing a line where warmup threads pin certain pages for long-running requests.

jamal: mitigation options I can kick off now: 1) force eviction (admin endpoint) 2) lower max_kv_cache_size for this node to 60% 3) enable immediate compaction patch (hotfix flag) and roll canary 4) temporarily route heavy embeddings/jobs off this node pool. Recommend 1+2 immediately.

emma: running forced-evict now (curl to admin). command: 
```
curl -s -XPOST "http://localhost:9001/admin/evict?mode=aggressive" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" 
```
Output: 
```
{"status":"ok","evicted_pages":18340,"reclaimed_bytes":"~14.2GB"}
```

emma: memory dropped ~12GB on prod-gpu-03, containers still up but latency spiked on a few routes (p95 450ms -> 900ms).

priya: good, that confirms fragmentation + evictable pages. side-effect as emma said — higher latency because eviction/populate traffic. we need a plan to stop the slow re-accumulation: aggressive evict buys time. for a durable fix we should enable the kvcache compactor and deploy the allocator patch that fixes bitmap compaction race.

rafael: customer impact — I pulled errors from SLO dashboard: three customers with >0.5% error increase in the last 2 hours: AcmeGames, NarrateAI, and AtlasSearch. I've pinged their CSEs and notified AMs. AcmeGames had a couple of timed-out streams; CS says they flagged users but no major outage yet.

jamal: I'm applying node-level config to reduce max_kv_cache_size on the pool and set eviction to aggressive for 1 hour. config snippet: 
```
{ "kvcache": { "max_percent": 60, "eviction_policy": "aggressive", "compactor_enabled": false } }
```
Applying to pool prod-pool-2 now.

pagerduty-bot: On-call rafael acknowledged INC-2026-0458. Estimated next check-in in 15m.

emma: note — one container on prod-gpu-03 restarted with CUDA error 700 after the evict (stack snippet): 
```
E cuda: cuLaunchKernel failed: error 700
E runtime: out of memory on device 0
  at runtime/main.cc:422
  at allocator/paged_attn.cc:1087
```
Node recovered and container auto-respawned by k8s. I'm watching for repeat.

priya: given repeated small OOMs, suggested short-term playbook: 1) keep aggressive eviction until compactor is rolled 2) throttle model sizes for routes that cause large warmups (route-level rate limit) 3) schedule a rolling restart with allocator patch (compaction fixes) and enable compactor on 5% canary first. I'll draft rollout steps.

alex: can we get a short handoff summary for the next oncall? include what we changed and what to watch. I'll send to the incident channel and patch the incident ticket.

jamal: handoff (for the record): - forced-evict ran at +2m -> reclaimed ~14GB - lowered max_kv_cache_size to 60% on prod-pool-2 - set eviction policy aggressive for 1h - alerted CS for impacted customers - watching for repeated cuMemAlloc(700) after evict - next steps: compactor canary + rolling restart.

rafael: next oncall please monitor: GPU memory resident_pages on prod-gpu-03/04, evict_rate (should be >1000 pages/min while aggressive), new CUDA 700 errors, and SLO error rates for AcmeGames/NarrateAI/AtlasSearch. If we see >3 OOM restarts in 30m, escalate to infra and consider temporarily draining the node pool.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-0458 status=mitigating. Actions: forced-evict applied, config updated, CS notified. Assigned owners: priya (fix rollout), jamal (mitigation), rafael (customer comms).

alex: leaving handoff to priya and jamal. tagging @next-oncall (do not escalate unless sustained OOMs or >1 customer outage).
